reasoning: The consulting ends in an agreed campaign arrangement (brief, media mix and schedule) that the agency works from and the client signs off. That is a checkable deliverable, so X's DISCRETE fits better than Y's INTERPERSONAL.

'Plan or conduct' joins two steps with separate handovers: a research plan or proposal that the client approves, and a findings report. Some specialists do only one of them. X splits on those handover points; Y treats the whole study as one project-sized item.

'Plans or materials' joins two different activities with different deliverables: a strategic communication plan, and individual pieces such as fact sheets or articles. X splits them and gives each a work item; Y's 'plan or material set' blends items of very different size.

'Plan or direct' joins two different activities. Planning yields a program plan that management approves (DISCRETE), and directing others' development and communication is supervision (INTERPERSONAL). Y splits them correctly; X folds the directing into the plan.

Posting to the website and posting to social media are the same activity, publishing ready content, done in different channels, so a split is not required. X's single DISCRETE part, one post or update published, is at the right level.
